newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks pare losses on Dow at close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks pare losses on Dow at close.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed marginally down on Thursday after drifting on thin volume in line with domestic economic data and developments on Wall Street, dealers and analysts said.
"The two markets began to move in step and afterwards there was profit-taking," said Carlos Fritsch, equity strategist at the Interacciones brokerage.

The leading IPC share index ended down 2.02 points, or 0.04 percent, at 5,014.61, but had reached as low as 4,997.70. The Dow Jones had meanwhile rebounded from an earlier low to end up 13.71 points at 7,942.03.

The bourse had opened sharply up in line with the Dow Jones in the wake of benign U.S. inflation data and received an additional boost from domestic industrial output figures before profit-taking set in, dealers said.
"As liquidity has dried up right now and thinned volume, dealers are taking profits," a floor trader said.
Trading volume was slower than for many recent sessions at 76 million shares.
Fritsch said market caution ahead of the August 19 Fed meeting had also cooled initial market enthusiasm.

"Everyone is waiting for August 19 to see if there is any tightening in U.S. monetary policy. We don't believe the Fed will announce any changes, but, even so, markets the world over, not just Mexico, have been following Wall Street closely," he said.
Dealers said Telefonos de Mexico, which has the heaviest weighting on the IPC, slowed down the market most, down 10 centavos to 20.10 pesos.
Conglomerate Alfa underpinned the market and ended up 50 centavos at 66.00 pesos after strong industrial output figures, dealers said.

The Finance Ministry released in early trade industrial production figures for June that were up 9.9 percent in year- on-year terms. A Reuters survey of Mexico City financial firms had predicted an average rise of 8.3 percent.
Despite the slide in blue chips, the broad market balance ended positive, with gainers outpacing decliners by 52 to 36 out of 108 stocks that changed hands.
